prompt: Stage 3-2 augment round, level 6, 48 gold, 74 HP, holding a pair of your 3-cost AD carry. You scouted and noted three things (see the scout panel). Which one changes what you do this round?

lobby.note: Has a 2-star of your 3-cost carry and two more copies on the bench
Lowest HP in the lobby, loss-streaking with 60 gold
Took an econ augment at 2-1, strong board

options.label: Seat 4 holding five copies of your carry: buy the copy in the shop now and decide at 4-1 whether the line is still open
Seat 2 at 38 HP: they will die early, so the lobby gets smaller and you can play slower
Seat 7's econ augment: they will out-scale you, so level now to stay ahead

explanation:
Five of eighteen copies sitting on one player's board and bench is the fact that changes a decision this round: the copy in your shop becomes worth buying immediately, because the pool is draining, and it starts a clock on whether you stay on this carry at all. That is a purchase and a plan you would not have made without the scout.

Seat 2's HP and Seat 7's augment are true and useless right now. A low player dying at 4-3 does not change your 3-2 shop, and an opponent's econ augment does not make leveling at 3-2 with 48 gold correct. Diamond scouting is not about noticing things; it is about spending the timer on the one thing that moves your hand.
principle: Scouting only counts when it changes a decision this round. Everything else is trivia.
commonMistake: Reacting to the scariest player instead of the player who is taking your units.
